page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.26xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance configured for workloads requiring massive memory footprints alongside large core counts. Powered by the KVM hypervisor on x86_64 architecture, this instance features 104 dedicated vCPUs provided by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. With 768.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers approximately 7.38 GB of RAM per vCPU, enabling extensive in-memory working sets without frequent disk paging.

Hardware specifications highlight an absence of local storage disks and zero hardware acceleration GPUs. System operations and persistent application data rely entirely on remote network storage volumes over a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. This network tier provides necessary throughput to support distributed architectures, continuous state synchronization, and cluster communications.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of dedicated cores combined with 768.0 GB of memory allows consolidation of extensive enterprise applications onto a single virtual node. The primary architectural tradeoff centers on the lack of direct-attached NVMe storage, meaning that overall I/O performance depends heavily on external storage provisioning. The instance is suited for enterprise relational databases, large-scale in-memory caching layers such as Redis or Memcached, distributed big data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise software.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.26xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for memory-heavy enterprise deployments. Running on a KVM hypervisor, it provides 104 dedicated vCPUs backed by 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processors and 768.0 GB of RAM, yielding roughly 7.38 GB of memory per vCPU. The server lacks local ephemeral storage and dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage architectures supported by a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. This networking capacity ensures sufficient throughput for distributed memory coordination, storage access, and synchronization across nodes. By offering a high allocation of dedicated compute and substantial memory density, it enables multi-instance consolidation. The server is well suited for large relational databases, in-memory caches, SAP deployments, ETL pipelines, and high-footprint data analytics engines.
